body.p: The Git History view shows the commit history, revision graph, commit details, and affected resources for the selected repository, branch, or resource. The view opens at the bottom of the application interface. You can open it in any of the following ways:

ul.li: Use the Show current repository history action from the toolbar of the Git Staging view.
Go to Window Show View Git History .
Use the Show history contextual action in supported views and editors.

section.title: Main Areas
section.p: The main areas in the Git History view are:

ul.li: Repository and branch header - Shows the repository name and the current branch.
Toolbar and text filter - Controls the history view.
History table - Shows the revision graph, commit messages, dates, authors, commit IDs, and uncommitted changes.
Commit details pane - Shows details for the selected commit.
Affected resources pane - Lists the files changed by the selected commit.

section.title: Toolbar and Filter
section.p: Use the toolbar to control which commits are shown in the history table.

ul.li: Branch Chooser - Choose All branches, All local branches, Current branch, or Current local branch.
Link with Editor - Synchronizes the history with the selected editor. It is enabled by default.
Refresh - Reloads the displayed history.
Text Filter - Filters the history by commit message, date, author, commit ID, branch name, or tag name.

section.title: History Table
section.p: The history table shows commits in rows. The graph column shows how commits are connected, and the other columns show the commit message, date, author, and commit ID.
For each commit in the history table, the following contextual menu actions are available:

p.note: To publish a new branch to the remote repository and start tracking that branch, push the local branch from the Git Staging view.

ul.li: Create tag - Marks the selected commit.
Merge - Merges the selected commit into the current branch.
Cherry-pick - Applies the selected commit to the current branch.
Checkout - Switches to the selected commit or creates a branch from it.
Revert commit - Creates a commit that undoes the selected commit.
Reset "[branch_name]" to this commit - Moves the branch to the selected commit.
Explain commit - Explains the selected commit with AI.

section.p: Select more than one commit to compare the changes across a range of revisions. The lower panes show the boundary commits and the files changed in the selected range.

When you select two or more committed revisions, the lower panes compare the newest and oldest selected commits. The left pane identifies the compared revisions, while the right pane lists all files changed between those two endpoints.
The contextual actions in the changed-files list depend on the change type:

ul.li: Modified and renamed files provide actions to compare the newer version with the older version and to open the newer, older, or working-copy version when available.
Added files provide actions to open the newer version and, when the file still exists locally, the working-copy version.
Deleted files provide an action to open the older version.

section.p: The history table can also show an Uncommitted changes row. Select it to inspect the working-copy changes that are not committed yet.

If you select the Uncommitted changes row together with one or more committed revisions, the lower panes compare the current working tree with the oldest selected revision. The left pane identifies the working tree and the selected revision, while the right pane lists all files that differ between them.

In this working-tree comparison mode, modified and renamed files can be compared directly with the selected revision, added files can be opened from the working copy, and deleted files can be opened at the selected revision.

When a range comparison produces no differences, the changed-files pane shows a No changes. message. When the Uncommitted changes row is selected by itself and there are no unstaged changes, the pane shows No unstaged changes..

section.title: Commit Details Pane
section.p: The commit details pane shows information about the selected commit. Use this pane to inspect the full commit ID, parent commit, author, date, committer, and commit message without opening another dialog box.

section.title: Affected Resources Pane
section.p: The affected resources pane lists the files changed by the selected commit. For each resource, the following contextual menu actions are available:

ul.li: Open (available for added and modified resources)
Open previous version (available for deleted resources)
Open working copy version (available for added and modified resources)
Reset file to this commit (available for added and modified resources)
Compare with previous version (available for modified resources)
Compare with working copy version (available for modified resources)
Compare with each other (available when selecting two versions of a single file)
